cases.name: Melissa A. "Missy" Lemerond Gray
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Missy was a graduate of Green Bay East High School where she was on the high honor roll. She continued her education at UW-Stout, also maintaining high honors status, earning a Bachelor's Degree in Psychology. After graduation from college, Missy moved to several locations across the United States, utilizing her education at various colleges as a resident counselor. Currently, Missy was employed at LLC Ruesch Properties as director of operations. Although Missy was a hard worker and enjoyed her work outside the home, her passion was being a mom and caretaker to her 2 beloved sons, Emmett and Avante.

Missy will be remembered as a selfless, kind-hearted person who always put others before herself. Shy by nature, Missy could be brought out of her bashfulness and flash you a smile that would light up the world. She was a champion for equal rights for all people. Her brother and sister knew that no matter what, they could always depend on Missy to lend an ear or hand. Missy was taken too soon from the people who loved her, but her family hopes that Missy is now resting peacefully. May her tragic death not be in vain, but bring awareness to domestic violence and perhaps help others that share similar stories."

cases.name: Paula O'Connor
cases.about:
Her Go Fund Me said, "She loved her work as a hairstylist, loved her family and adored visiting her Grandchildren."

Her obituary said, "Paula was known to bring joy to those around her, love life, laugh, and make others laugh. Paula spent her life as a wonderful mother first, and as a career hairstylist at her salon. She leaves behind a loving family, and many friends and clients. While raising three children of her own with their Father Shawn O'Connor, she also took in and loved multiple foster children, including Amber and Christine Kaslow, and Miranda Young. Paula's love for Family extended to her Grandchildren. Paula never missed a chance to speak about how proud she was of her children and grandchildren. Often visiting her daughter and her grandchildren in Florida, and her son and granddaughter in Indianapolis. Paula loved her time spent Up North at her families ancestral property on Glade lake. Even desiring to be laid to rest there, with other family. She had plans and dreams for her land, and was working to improve and develop it. She had artistic talents for design, decorating, renovation, and painting. As well as a passion for food and cooking."
